chief_complaint: pearly facial bump with telangiectasias that bleeds
hpi_details: A 41-year-old male presents to the clinic with pearly facial bump with telangiectasias that bleeds. The patient states the symptoms started recently and have been gradually worsening, accompanied by generalized fatigue.
ideas: He thinks the bump is an ingrown beard hair or a stubborn shaving cut that keeps reopening every time he shaves.
concerns: He is worried that the bleeding sore might be a form of skin cancer like the one his uncle had surgically removed.
expectations: He hopes the doctor will inspect it closely and refer him to a specialist to remove it neatly without leaving a huge scar.

clinical_knowledge.topic: Basal Cell Carcinoma evaluation and management
core_concepts: Prompt recognition and structured assessment of Basal Cell Carcinoma is essential for guiding targeted diagnostic workup and clinical decision-making.
A thorough clinical history, baseline risk assessment, and targeted objective testing must be synthesized rather than relying on any single symptom in isolation.
Standard management emphasizes Plan for Basal Cell Carcinoma cheek: Punch biopsy, wide local surgical excision or Mohs surgery, adapted to individual patient risk factors and clinical severity.
Diagnostic workup and therapeutic decisions should adhere to established clinical guidelines while accounting for patient-specific comorbidities.

Prematurely discharging or reassuring the patient before completing appropriate diagnostic assessment.
Initiating empirical treatment without considering major patient contraindications or drug interactions.

must_ask.say: Does the bump have a pearly, shiny appearance with visible small blood vessels?
Does it bleed easily, even with minor trauma?
How has this changed over time?
How much sun exposure have you had over the years?
How long have you had this?

history.answer: I have a small pimple-like bump on my right cheek that started bleeding easily whenever I wash my face or shave.
I first noticed it about two or three months ago, and it has not gone away.
It is right here on my right cheek, right in the middle of my face.
It started as a tiny bump and has been gradually getting slightly larger over the past few weeks.
It is about five or six millimeters across, and it is the only one I have seen.
It feels like a firm little bead under the skin, and it does not feel soft or squishy.
No, it does not hurt at all, even when I press right on it.
It looks shiny and almost pearly pink, and I can see tiny little red blood vessel threads running across it.
Yes, it bleeds with minimal touching like towel drying, forms a small crust, and then bleeds again without ever healing.
No, there is no redness around it, no warmth, and no foul-smelling drainage.
No, there is no blackhead or central hole, and nothing like white cheesy material has ever come out of it.
No, it does not swell up and shrink back down; it has just stayed there and grown very slowly.
No, I never had an injury, surgery, cyst, or bad acne in that exact spot.
No fever, no chills, no night sweats, and my weight has been completely steady.
I have been feeling somewhat worn out and generally fatigued lately, but I think that is mostly from work stress.
I have spent quite a bit of time outdoors over the years without sunscreen, and I got a few bad sunburns when I was younger.
I have never had skin cancer before, and neither have my parents or siblings.
No, I have never had an organ transplant, I do not take steroid pills, and I am not immunocompromised.
I tried squeezing it once thinking it was an ordinary pimple, but only a drop of blood came out, so I stopped messing with it.
I thought it was just a stubborn shaving cut or an ingrown whisker that keeps opening back up every time I shave.
My uncle had to have a dangerous skin cancer cut out of his cheek, so I'm terrified this might be something malignant like that.
I'd like you to take a close look at it and refer me to a skin specialist if it needs to be taken off.
I do not have any chronic medical conditions like high blood pressure or diabetes.
I have never had any surgeries and I have never been hospitalized.
I do not take any prescription medications, over-the-counter pills, or herbal supplements.
I do not have any allergies to medications, foods, or latex.
I have never smoked cigarettes or used tobacco products.
I have an occasional beer or glass of wine with friends on weekends, nothing heavy.
I work in construction management, spending several hours outside each week, and I live with my wife.

exam.finding: Blood pressure is 120/78 mmHg, heart rate is 72 beats per minute, respiratory rate is 14 breaths per minute, temperature is 36.7 degrees Celsius, and oxygen saturation is 99% on room air.
Well-nourished, alert male who appears comfortable and in no acute distress.

A solitary 6 mm pearly, pinkish-white papule on the right cheek with prominent branching telangiectasias, slightly rolled borders, and a tiny central scab that is non-tender and non-fluctuant; no other abnormal lesions elsewhere on the skin.
No palpable or tender preauricular, submandibular, or cervical lymph nodes.
Conjunctivae are pink without pallor, and sclerae are anicteric.
